court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Principal Family Court Judge, Chennai - H.M.O.P.No.2222 of 2023
case_name: Preethi v. Vinay Kumar — C.M.A.No.306 of 2024
facts_of_case: The petitioner-wife filed a petition seeking decree of nullity of the marriage under section 12(1)(a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The respondent-husband did not allow her to talk with her parents and behaved rudely. They stayed in Nellore for 2 months after their marriage before leaving India and working in U.K.

legal_principles.principle: A respondent's deliberate absence from the trial court can be considered as an indirect admission of the facts pleaded by the appellant.
legal_principles.held: The respondent-husband did not come to court to deny the facts narrated by the appellant-wife, it is an indirect admission that the marriage was not consummated.

legal_principles.principle: A respondent's refusal to consummate the marriage can be considered as cruelty to a young spouse.
legal_principles.held: The respondent did not come to court to deny the facts narrated by the appellant-wife, it is an indirect admission that the marriage was not consummated.

outcome.final_order: The final court order set aside the judgment and decree dated 09.01.2024 made by the Principal Family Court Judge, Chennai.

keywords: Latin maxim: Ubi Jus, Ibi Remedium
use_for_drafting: drafting a divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
